reviews.text: Love them especially Jennifer and Elizabeth . I like Dr Hoffmans cautious approach.

I always schedule my appointments first thing in the mornings so it hasn't been an issue for me, but the parking looks like it can be a little tricky as it's fairly small lot.

The staff and the doctor were so nice and friendly. I did not have to wait at all upon arriving for our appointment. They treated my dog with so much kindness and compassion. I will 100% make this my dog’s new primary care clinic.

Dr Grasmehr is wonderful. Highly recommended. Excellent judgment. Great with our animals. And with the humans accompanying them as well. Contrary to many other vets we have dealt with she does not over order but deals with each situation individually.

This place is amazing! I truly am overwhelmed with my experience and I’m looking forward to having a caring and intelligent team as I navigate my little ones golden years!

Very capable and courteous staff.

The office was clean and orderly and the veterinarian was very caring and prescribed the proper treatment and my dog was cured of his cough.
Taking care of my puppers for over 20 years.  Simply the best.
Finally found a Dr. that resolved a long standing problem. Went through several Dr.   Im very happy my baby is getting better.. Thank you 😊

Very upsetting experience. I had purposely selected Dr. Hoffman to see my adult cat for the first time. I have been in pet care many years, and had taken  my client's dog for a visit a couple years back. Was impressed with her. My vet closed this last year with no notice. SO...I remembered that experience and made an appt. online maybe 4/5 days in advance for my kitty. It was for 3:30. I walked in about 3:20/25 (with a very unhappy cat in carrier). I said hello and the girl behind the counter said she'd be right with me (she was on the phone). Another girl walked in and out from the back a few times. There were no other people in the wait area. A couple people came in and picked up meds etc. By the time it was 3:40/45... I took my upset cat and walked out. NO ONE EVER ACKNOWLEDGED MY PRESENCE after the initial glance. No one ever followed up to see what had happened. My guess is Dr. Hoffman knows nothing of this. I DO hope she reads this.

They always take very good care of my fur babies. I've been a client since they bought the practice and highly recommend them. Dr. Hoffman is very caring and knowledgeable. Vinny was having his 1st exam and they treated him so well, that he was so happy to be back at his 3 month visit!

The care my dogs have received from Dr. Hoffman has been exemplary. Not only is Dr. Hoffman a brilliant vet, she is one of the most caring women I know. She promptly notifies me of test results with long detailed explanations that I can understand. Treatment is always geared toward what is best for my dogs physically and emotionally. I highly recommend her.
They are the best!!

TARZANA PET CLINIC has been our veterinary clinic for over 20 years.
Drs. Hoffman, Grasmehr and Swann are outstanding!  They’re excellent clinicians and equally important—are kind, caring, compassionate, and gentle with one’s pets(as well as us humans who entrust our beloved pets to them ; )   Your pet could not be in better hands, when health issues arise.

The staff is caring and efficient.

The physical plant is immaculate.

We highly recommend TARZANA PET CLINIC.

I had an HORRIBLE experience at Tarzana Pet Clinic. They advertise that new/first-time clients receive a complimentary exam when booking an appointment, which is exactly why I scheduled with them.

My small poodle had a broken nail and was clearly in pain. I booked the earliest same-day appointment they had available, which ended up being later in the evening, so my dog spent the entire day waiting to be seen.

After checking in and being taken to the exam room, the manager suddenly told me, “Since your dog is injured, it will be a $120 exam fee.” My mouth dropped. This was never disclosed when booking, despite the advertised complimentary exam on their website and even in the appointment confirmation email I received.

I wasted my entire day waiting while my dog was uncomfortable and in pain, only to find out at the appointment that the advertised offer apparently didn’t apply. If there are exclusions or emergency/injury fees, they should be clearly stated upfront instead of surprising people after they arrive.

Very disappointed. It felt misleading and like money came before transparency or patient care.

I made an appointment with a vet technician for Frankie, because he was due for his rabies shot. We also opted for a cytopoint refresher, as he was pretty itchy due to allergies. Frankie is 15 and the sweetest senior pug, but if there is anything he hates, it's getting his nails trimmed. He has a partially collapsed trachea, so moving quickly or stressful situations make it harder for him to breathe and cause coughing. Getting his nails trimmed professionally or at the vet  has been too stressful in the past. Sadly, I resorted to sneaking up during his naps to clip one or two nails before he would wake up. During his latest visit the technician suggested a nail trim. I agreed, but cautioned about his condition. To my delight, they were able to trim all his nails beautifully while he was standing on his own (instead of being held)!! We obviously love Dr. Grasmehr, but this was a wonderful opportunity to highlight the excellent work and care of the technicians and staff in the office, and I'm happy to do so.

I explained we were just back in town (we live part time in another country where we also regularly see a vet), and would book an appointment soon, but asked for an exception to be made to refill the prescription to bridge the gap between running out and coming in for the next wellness check. They ignored two emails and still denied the Chewy prescription refill request. We ran out of the medication, which was not in the best interest of my dogs health. I realize I should've been more on top of my timing, but the disregard for my pet's health and complete lack of communication was upsetting. It's been a week and I still haven't heard back from them. As a pet owner and client, that's unacceptable.

Ten Stars to Tarzana Pet Clinic and Dr. Swann !

Our beautiful Bella🐈, the light of our lives, suddenly stopped eating.  Nothing seemed to whet her appetite — every conceivable high-end gravy cat food, lox, rotisserie chicken strips — nothing. Our vet in Northridge seemed to have gone awol.  We got desperate; and then my hubby’s friend, Matt, recommended his vet Dr. Swann, right down the block at Tarzana Pet Clinic.   They very generously squeezed us in — normally new patients have a wait.

When we arrived, the front desk team and the Vet staff were wonderful with Bella.

Dr. Swann almost immediately could feel our darling had a large abdominal mass 😢😭, almost certainly liver cancer, as she had yellow lip linings.  We set out a plan of an X-ray before doing bloodwork because, Dr. Swann, explained that we could ascertain whether she had digestive function and perhaps some time left or we’d need to kiss her goodbye that day.  The bloodwork became unnecessary … terminal is terminal.  We were not “sold” to double check.

The X-ray revealed she had functionality, and we decided to hydrate her and giver her appetite steroids.   We also knew this would only give her a few weeks to a month of a comfortable goodbye.  During the next few weeks, they helped us over the phone.  Luckily, Bella got her dancing shoes back on; and she celebrated a few veer happy, joyful weeks and a special Valentine’s Day with us.

Bella crossed the rainbow bridge, peacefully, last night.  We had a post mortem today, President’s Day, with Dr, Swann.  He said she crossed over without pain and where she felt love.

We can’t thank Dr. Swann and the staff at Tarzana Pet Clinic enough for their help during these past few very, very difficult weeks.

I highly recommend avoiding this clinic. They always refuse to give my dog his allergy shots, insisting he needs to see the vet first, even though he’s been getting the same shots for months! Every time I reluctantly agree to do the vet exam, because i’m desperate for the cytopoint allergy shot, the vet sees him and just tells me “Oh yeah it’s been a very bad allergy season”, and then proceeds to recommend the same shot that I am already visiting for in the first place. The vet visit is always just a money grab, with the doctor doing absolutely nothing except confirming that my dog needs the shot, which we already know. On top of overcharging for everything, they also always make sure to add a random “waste fee”.

Since switching to a different vet, the difference has been incredible! Not only did they charge a fair price for the allergy shots, without all the unnecessary steps, but they also didn’t try to rip me off with a bunch of extra fees. This clinic is way overpriced and seems more focused on making a quick buck than providing real care for pets. Save your money and go somewhere that actually values your time and pet.

I contacted this clinic months in advance to ensure I would have all the necessary paperwork to take my cat to Europe. They scheduled an appointment 5 business days before my flight and, without informing me beforehand, charged me $700 for a health certificate. At the appointment, they only checked my cat’s weight and temperature, then printed the certificate for me to mail to the USDA. I repeatedly told them that, according to the USDA website, the certificate must be submitted electronically by the accredited veterinarian. Despite this, they insisted it was my responsibility to submit it.

After numerous calls, I finally spoke with the office manager, who confirmed that I had to mail the certificate myself, along with additional documents I didn’t even have—documents the clinic should have provided. When I explained I only had 4 business days left and this process wasn’t feasible, the office manager suggested I go in person to the USDA office in El Segundo. Thankfully, when I called El Segundo, they told me they don’t handle this and that I’d have to go to Sacramento! I live in LA, so this was entirely unrealistic.

When I contacted the USDA directly, they confirmed that the vet should have submitted the certificate electronically through the USDA’s system, and that it was outrageous to charge $700 just to print a document. The USDA explained this likely happened because the clinic didn’t want to handle the submission themselves.

Frustrated, I went back to the clinic and demanded to meet with the office manager in person. She admitted that her team didn’t organize the process properly and that their clinic didn’t have the system to submit certificates—an unbelievable oversight for an accredited veterinarian. She also confirmed they had failed to disclose the $700 charge in advance. She acknowledged their mistakes but offered no immediate solution. I requested a refund, explaining how stressful this was since I had no one to care for my cat while I was away, and this situation was entirely avoidable had they followed proper procedures.

That same day, I contacted another veterinarian who confirmed the first clinic should never have printed the certificate without submitting it. This second clinic handled everything efficiently and had my certificate approved by the USDA by Friday—it was Tuesday when I contacted them.

This clinic’s team is unqualified and completely unhelpful. They showed no concern for their mistakes or the stress they caused. Charging $700 to essentially do nothing, without even disclosing the fee, is unacceptable. I had to fight to even speak with someone in charge, and their solution was entirely impractical. I will not return and cannot recommend this clinic to anyone.
Tarzana PET Clinic is the best pet clinic around. I have been to many clinics over 40 years of having cats. The vets are very knowledgeable and kind.
